title: Record S12's post-merge review and its six fixes
message: Record S12's post-merge review and its six fixes

title: Keep a captain's waypoints and routes to that captain
message:
Keep a captain's waypoints and routes to that captain

S12 let only a row's creator change it but let every captain use it,
which coupled captains two ways. A captain could put another's
waypoint on a route, after which its creator could never delete it.
And a route's creator could change the course of another captain's
hull scheduled on that route, since a scheduled hull rebuilds her
route from the cache at each departure.

A captain may now sail (setroute), schedule (setschedule), list, and
route through only their own waypoints and routes and the harbors'
(creator 0); immortals may use any. Name lookups take the caller's
own row, then the harbors', then the first, which they refuse. The
rule lives in two helpers, autopilot_may_change() and
autopilot_may_use(). Help (DELWAYPOINT, DELROUTE, ADDTOROUTE,
SETROUTE, SETSCHEDULE, LISTROUTES, LISTWAYPOINTS) in both places,
VESSEL_SYSTEM.md, the player guide, and the rules gate (Vesselmate
is now refused Kohdee's route and waypoint for use too).

title: Stop the manifest writer at a failure only inside a transaction
message:
Stop the manifest writer at a failure only inside a transaction

2ba35d6b1 made vessel_db_save_cargo() return at its first failed
INSERT, to keep a lost connection inside a trade's transaction from
committing later lots on their own. Its other callers save without a
transaction, after the manifest's DELETE has already committed, so
every later lot was now lost with the failing one. It stops early only
when the connection is in a transaction (SERVER_STATUS_IN_TRANS),
and otherwise writes every lot it can, as before.

title: Count Connector/C's 5000-range client errors as an unanswered COMMIT
message:
Count Connector/C's 5000-range client errors as an unanswered COMMIT

trade_commit() took only client errors 2000-2999 for a COMMIT the
server never answered, but MariaDB Connector/C also reports client
network errors in 5000-5999 (CR_ERR_NET_READ 5013, CR_ERR_NET_WRITE
5014). Such a failure after the server committed was taken for a
refused trade: no second write, and the hold restored against a
database that held the trade. The log line for a trade that cannot be
settled now names the port supply as well as the manifest.

title: Give a removed player's waypoints and routes to the staff
message:
Give a removed player's waypoints and routes to the staff

Waypoint and route ownership is keyed on the player's ID, and boot
sets top_idnum to the highest ID left in the index, so permanently
removing the highest-numbered player hands that ID, and their
waypoints and routes, to the next new character.
vessel_handle_player_removal() looks the ID up (the player is still in
the index when remove_player() calls it) and, in its cleanup
transaction, sets the player's rows to creator 0, in the caches too.

title: Create ship_waypoints and ship_routes with their creator column
message:
Create ship_waypoints and ship_routes with their creator column

init_vessel_system_tables() created both tables without creator_id,
which only boot's vessel_ownership_ensure_schema() added. Tables made
through the staff 'init vessels' path after boot lacked it until the
next reboot, so every setwaypoint and createroute INSERT failed.
